title: [BUG] Claude clobbers correct typographic marks and can't be told otherwise
body:
## Environment
- Platform (select one):
  - [x] Anthropic API
  - [ ] AWS Bedrock
  - [ ] Google Vertex AI
  - [ ] Other: <!-- specify -->
- Claude CLI version: 1.0.11
- Operating System: macOS 15.3.1
- Terminal:  ghostty

## Bug Description
When suggesting significant edits to files, Claude will decide to "fix" already-correct typographic marks (and thus making them incorrect).

For example, I have a user-facing string in my code that says `I’m`, and Claude (when editing unrelated code) does a drive-by that replaces it with `I'm`. I've tried adding custom instructions in `CLAUDE.md` asking it to do the exact opposite (because I generally *want* to use the correct typographic marks!), but even though Claude can *identify* that it isn't following the rules, when trying to fix the issue, it justs spit out a bunch of the same error:

`Error: No changes to make: old_string and new_string are exactly the same.`

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ask Claude to make significant changes to a file that has Unicode typographical marks in it (proper apostrophes/curly quotes)
2. Claude will reduce a single apostrophe to a foot mark ('), and curly quotes to inch marks (").

## Expected Behavior
Claude should not try to change the unrelated strings and leave them as they are. Ideally it would do the *opposite* in my case -- finding instances of user-facing text or comments that use the incorrect versions and update them accordingly.

## Actual Behavior
Claude clobbers the correct code, forcing me to address the diff before committing the code.
author: aardvarkk

## Confirming on Linux + Critical Impact in Perl

I can confirm this bug also affects **Linux** (Fedora 42), not just macOS. The impact in our Perl codebase was severe:

### Impact
- **502 lines** of multi-language UI text corrupted in one file alone
- **Critical**: In Perl, converting `'` (U+2019) to `'` (U+0027) **breaks string literals**:

```perl
# Before (works):
$text = "Nom d'hôte";  # Single string with U+2019

# After Edit tool (syntax error):
$text = "Nom d'hôte";  # Interpreted as: "N
